entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Aleksander Krzysztof Naruszewicz was a Polish nobleman who served as the Deputy Chancellor of Lithuania from 1658 to 1667. His significance lies in his role as a key figure in the political landscape of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth during the 17th century. As a representative of the nobility, he played a crucial part in the negotiations with the Swedish Empire, which led to the Treaty of Oliva in 1660, a significant event in the history of the region.

Naruszewicz was born in 1632 in Wilno, Lithuania (now Vilnius, Lithuania), and died on June 21, 1668. He was a member of the Polish nobility and held various positions, including that of a delegate to the Polish Sejm.

His legacy can be seen in the continued influence of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth on the political and cultural landscape of Eastern Europe. The Treaty of Oliva, which he helped negotiate, marked a significant turning point in the history of the region, as it established a temporary peace between the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth and the Swedish Empire.

In the words of the Polish historian, 'Naruszewicz was a skilled diplomat who played a crucial role in maintaining the balance of power in the region.'
